features.fullDescription: 17th or early 18th century, vernacular 2 storey, crowstepped building with single storey wings, slated roof, rubble and ashlar dressings, incorporating earlier work, ie doorway with key-blocked lintel and jamb-blocks with paterae. Outside stone stair to 1st floor level on the North side of the building. Extensive garden walls, that to the west of the main house has clairvoie with early 19th century cast iron railings, otherwise rubble with rough triangular cope. The wall ends against the Priest's House. Attached to the North East corner of Kemback Beg is a secondary wall with a slated out building and a former dovecote incorporated. This wall also ends against the Priest's House.

features.fullDescription: Later 18th century, three storey, rubble with projecting ashlar dressings, gabled, straight skews with caretto moulded skewputs, slated, droved ashlar rectangular end-stacks with caretto cornice. South front, 3 bay, centre door in round-headed opening with fanlight, tall round-headed openings lighting ground and 1st floors to left and right, similar opening lighting 1st and 2nd floors centre 1st floor. Small rectangular opening second floor right. End elevations have, off centre, a single tall round-headed opening through ground and 1st and small round-headed opening at 2nd floor. North, rear, elevation has tall round-headed window to right through ground and 1st and 2nd floors, chimney gablet over. Two small later? rectangular openings at ground floor left. Inside, the rooms are plain and altered but those on the 1st floor have their original cornices and six panelled doors. Circular newel stair.

features.fullDescription: 1814, Gothick, 3 bay rectangle with later single storey porch at S end. Gabled slated, coursed squared and droved rubble, droved ashlar dressings and plinth. Bellcote at S gable: single gothic arch on each face carrying spirelet with crocketted finial. West front: three tall gothic windows with set back chamfered reveals, Y-tracery carried on slender clustered shafts, further subdivided by astragals, intersecting at head. 2 similar windows in North wall. East and south walls windowless. Interior: gallery to South, pulpit in NE corner. Simple plasterwork includes cornice and small round-headed niche at N end of S wall.

features.fullDescription: Earlier 18th century with near contemporary additions. Substantial baronial additions 1907. Originally 3 storey, 3 window wide by one window deep, droved ashlar rectangle with a Gibbsian doorpiece, raised angle, window and eaves margins and a piended roof with tall rectangular end-stacks on curvilinear gablets, extended W by one bay and returned North forming an L-plan house with symmetrical 5 window W front with closer spaced windows but otherwise identically detailed with the earlier work. 1907 work included the addition of crowstepped gablets at centres of East and West fronts and on the South front a crow-stepped porch with coat of arms, a turret at the SE angle and most importantly the left hand bay was pushed out as a lower advanced wing. Internally most of the plain 18th century work survives including a good scale-and- platt cantilever stair, the alterations of 1907 have no particular distinction.
